title: PlacementKind
description: The closed list of placement kinds: what a need asks to have carried and what a posture offers to carry. One deterministic `decide` pass covers every kind, so a carrier's capacity is charged across kinds in the charter's serve order (interfaces spec §D.1). A new kind is four coupled steps landed together: a variant here and in `placement_core::KindId`, a `PlacementKind` implementation in the crate that owns the carrier, a `grant-scope` entry if it spends compute, and a probe (§D.1 'Extension'). Closed rather than open because the compute-grant scopes a kind consumes are a closed list. Source of truth: this schema; Rust mirror `placement_core::KindId` (elohim/placement/core/src/kind.rs, `#[non_exhaustive]`, kebab-case serde). TypeScript constants only: `_codegen` (no `rust` key, so codegen-rs writes nothing) and never `_dna`, so no constant reaches content_store_integrity and no DNA hash moves (interfaces spec §2.G, G11). placement-core's schema_contract test reads this file with include_str! and compares it, in order, with `KindId::ALL`, a list kept by hand in kind.rs. It catches a value changed here, but a variant added to `KindId` without extending `ALL` still passes: no exhaustive match ties `ALL` to the enum, and the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]` (follow-on: a guard in kind.rs that matches every variant against its index in `ALL`).
